about: Decisions the main agent made on its own authority, with what it recommended and where each stands. Andrew, 2026-11-11: "just be proactive and do what you need to do; make a decisions.json file with all your decisions and what you recommended and just do things and get blaze to work". A decision here is reversed by Andrew saying so; one that changes a rule also changes tools/agents/rules.ts.

decisions.decision: Lanes with their own ix VM build, check and test their own work. Merges to main, measurements that claims rest on, persisted-state and bootstrap changes, and the check before a merge stay with the main agent.
decisions.why: The round trip through the main agent cost 10 to 40 minutes per fix all day; a lane with a VM closes the loop in minutes.
decisions.recommended: Yes, for the speed lanes first.

decisions.decision: One new blaze built from today's tree becomes the compiler for all work (a blaze built earlier is a legal stage 0). It is used on the VMs as soon as stage 2 passes; a release follows when main's gate is green.
decisions.why: The old release has its own faults and does not know the lint ratchet or the language extensions; most of the day's detours came from building with it.
decisions.state: in progress: stage 2 running on two VMs

decisions.decision: "Compiles" means `blaze check` with tests on the exact tip, by a blaze that knows the tree's rules, before a merge.
decisions.why: Main was merged on a library build by the old release; its daemon tests and its own lint check did not pass.

decisions.decision: A crate with no line in a lint baseline is unmeasured (held at warn until a bless records it), not zero. Vendored third-party crates and the std-only script crates are exempt from blaze's own style lints by rule.
decisions.why: A new crate could not pass the check, so could not be blessed, so could never get a line; 3,931 lint errors in script and vendored crates stopped the tree's own check.
decisions.state: partly done: 89 crates listed unmeasured by hand on edit-all-1111; the rule change in blaze-lints and blaze-units is to do

decisions.decision: Memory is a first priority beside edit latency: front-end results become store records read through the pool, and the allocator returns freed memory.
decisions.why: Memory stopped work three times on 2026-11-11 (58 GB for one crate's tests, 81 GiB for blaze building blaze, 61 to 71 GB on reth and tempo); the same change fixes edits after a restart.
decisions.state: to start once the new compiler exists

decisions.decision: The optimizer's tier bars may be measured against rustc -O0, -O1 and -O3 in the optimizer's benchmark harness only. rustc stays out of every correctness path and every build.
decisions.why: A Pareto claim needs a reference point; rule verify-on-real-projects forbids rustc as an oracle, not as a stopwatch for a published benchmark.
decisions.recommended: Yes, as a narrow exception written into the rule when the harness is built.
decisions.state: decided; the rule text changes with the harness (ledger B20)

decisions.decision: Release builds keep the linker's patch room (as file holes).
decisions.why: The file-level splice that makes release edit-links fast uses it at every optimization level.

decisions.decision: blaze's checkout of a git dependency carries a deterministic, synthesized .git that real git can read.
decisions.why: cargo's checkout has one and build scripts (vergen) run git there; a stub that answers one command and breaks another is worse than none.
decisions.recommended: Build it as its own spec-then-build piece.

decisions.decision: bstd's unsynced renames issue a truly unsynced rename on real drivers too.
decisions.why: That is their documented contract; callers relying on the stronger behaviour are the bugs the simulation exists to find; nothing runs on bstd yet.

decisions.decision: `strip` in a profile is accepted with a named note on every build until the linker honours it (ledger D44); it is not refused.
decisions.why: Real projects set it; refusing would stop builds the reference compiler accepts.
decisions.state: written on inv-fix-1111 and verified; to merge

decisions.decision: A missed loader probe is not part of a pure build script's key: a library appearing later at a probed path does not invalidate the kept run.
decisions.why: Same class as system libraries, which are not keyed either; tightening it needs a design for runtime inputs as a whole.

decisions.decision: The Python fixture generator is ported once into blaze-script as its one home, together with the harness scripts that use it; loop_syscalls.py stays on the allowed list until then.
decisions.why: A second copy of the fixture in Rust would be two homes for one concept.
decisions.state: to do with the harness batch

decisions.decision: bv_decide (Lean.ofReduceBool) is allowed for bit-vector rule proofs only, in files the MIR proofs cannot import, listed by the gate.
decisions.why: Andrew, 2026-11-11: yes to "yes, but kept separate".
decisions.state: done on rule-lang-1111: the gate enforces it; 3 of 248 theorems use it

decisions.decision: Builds by the released blaze that fault (the forged-id panic, a loop stall) are retried by the VM scripts, each retry printed with its cause, until the use-after-release behind the panic is found.
decisions.why: The panic happens from a clean database, so clearing state is not a fix; a loud retry keeps work moving without hiding it.
decisions.recommended: Retry loudly; find the cause on the new compiler.

decisions.decision: One large ix VM per concurrent heavy job (bootstrap, target projects, verification, a building lane); a VM is removed when its job ends.
decisions.why: Verification capacity, not writing, was the day's bottleneck; a 62 GB VM was OOM-killed and one VM lost its disk.
decisions.state: in force: rework-b (bootstrap), rework-t (reth, tempo), rework-d, rework-e, rework-s

decisions.decision: A branch is admin-merged to main when its own content is verified on a VM, in small pieces as each goes green, rather than held for one large merge.
decisions.why: Andrew, 2026-11-11: "can we admin merge anything in as well". Long-lived unmerged branches were the source of the semantic conflicts that broke main.
decisions.recommended: Merge what is verified now: the invariant controls with the strip note and the nostd port; the lint baselines; the three compiler fixes (memory budget, loader reads, effect-check binder) once stage 2 passes with them.

decisions.decision: The scheduler is redesigned as one graph of pure, identity-keyed nodes pulled by what is waited for: cycles as single nodes, no shared mutable state in a node, priority from who waits, cores and memory both admitted, built for hundreds of cores (docs/v2/plan/design/scheduler.md). Built in the order of measured cost, summaries and the two codegen locks first.
decisions.why: Andrew, 2026-11-11: "redesign the whole scheduler", "needs to work on 100s of cores". A release build of blaze by blaze kept 17 to 43 of 64 cores busy; about 30% of its CPU was one pass redone by many threads; two locks cost 6,555 thread-seconds.
decisions.recommended: Yes; keep the pool, fibers and slots of the 2026-11-02 plan and replace the model above them.

decisions.decision: build, run and test default to the edit goal: tier 0 code first, optimized code made in the background and patched in; the max goal waits for optimized code. The goal and the promotion's progress are on every status line.
decisions.why: Andrew, 2026-11-11: "by default we should start with a debug build and then in the background try to get more optimized, like a JIT"; Relax (makepad) publishes 50 to 200 ms save-to-patch with this shape.
decisions.recommended: Yes, as step 7 of the scheduler design; one goal setting replaces the two tier settings the tree has.

decisions.decision: A statement of fact rests on a tool call of the session; rule claims-from-evidence.
decisions.why: The agent said LLVM was most of an 80-minute build without a query; the profile said about 13%.

decisions.decision: Interim: cargo with the pinned nightly builds, checks and unit-tests blaze in the dev loop, and a cargo-built blaze is a legal stage 0; blaze still builds blaze daily and for releases, and every claim about blaze's behaviour is measured with a blaze.
decisions.why: Andrew, 2026-11-11: "ideally we can build with cargo until blaze is fast". cargo check passes after three small fixes; a release build takes 292 s on the Mac against about 80 minutes and 175 GB for blaze building blaze.
decisions.recommended: Yes, with the conditions in rule blaze-builds-blaze; back to blaze-only when a warm self-rebuild is under a minute.
decisions.state: done: rule changed; the cargo-built blaze of all-1111 runs hello-world on macOS

decisions.decision: The bar is makepad's Relax, measured head to head on one machine and kept in the gate, and blaze has to be categorically better: a body edit patched in under 20 ms, a save rerunning only the tests it reaches, a cold start that is a download from a store shared across machines, optimized code faster than rustc --release, hundreds of cores, the whole language.
decisions.why: Andrew, 2026-11-11: "we strictly need better compile times and faster code than our competitor", "we need to be categorically better". Relax publishes 50 to 200 ms save-to-patch and optimized code 1.14 to 2.29 times slower than rustc --release.
decisions.recommended: Yes; these are targets, none is measured yet.
